symptoms.symptom: Surface elements do not work properly

causes.label: Cooktop controls improperly set.
remedies: Check to see the correct control is set for the surface element you are using.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Cooktop controls improperly set."

causes.label: Incorrect cleaning methods being used.
remedies: Use recommended cleaning procedures.
See the Cleaning the glass cooktop section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Incorrect cleaning methods being used."

causes.label: Cookware with rough bottoms being used or coarse particles (salt or sand) were between the cookware and the surface of the cooktop.
remedies: To avoid scratches, use the recommended cleaning procedures.
Make sure bottoms of cookware are clean before use, and use cookware with smooth bottoms.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Cookware with rough bottoms being used or coarse particles (salt or sand) were between the cookware and the surface of the cooktop."

causes.label: Cookware has been slid across the cooktop surface.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Cookware has been slid across the cooktop surface."

symptoms.symptom: Areas of discoloration on the cooktop

causes.label: Food spillovers not cleaned before next use.
remedies: See the Cleaning the glass cooktop section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Food spillovers not cleaned before next use."

causes.label: Hot surface on a model with a light-colored glass cooktop.
remedies: This is normal.
The surface may appear discolored when it is hot.
This is temporary and will disappear as the glass cools.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Hot surface on a model with a light-colored glass cooktop."

causes.label: Hot cooktop came into contact with plastic placed on the hot cooktop.
remedies: See the Glass surface – potential for permanent damage section in the Cleaning the glass cooktop section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Hot cooktop came into contact with plastic placed on the hot cooktop."

causes.label: Hot sugar mixture spilled on the cooktop.
remedies: Call a qualified technician for replacement.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Hot sugar mixture spilled on the cooktop."

symptoms.symptom: Frequent cycling off and on of surface elements

causes.label: Improper cookware being used.
remedies: Use only flat cookware to minimize cycling.
See the Radiant surface elements section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Improper cookware being used."

causes.label: Keypad is dirty.
remedies: Clean the keypad.

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

causes.label: Improper cookware being used.
remedies: Use a flat, metallic pan that is 4.0″ or larger.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Improper cookware being used."

causes.label: Pan is improperly placed.
remedies: Make sure the pan is centered on the corresponding surface element.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Pan is improperly placed."

causes.label: Cooktop control improperly set.
remedies: Check to see that the control is set properly.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Cooktop control improperly set."

causes.label: Cooktop too hot and the time-out feature activated.
remedies: Allow the surface element(s) to cool for 1/2 to 1 hour before using again.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Cooktop too hot and the time-out feature activated."

symptoms.symptom: Surface element is glowing red when it should be on a low power setting

causes.label: The rapid heat-up feature activated.
remedies: The cooktop has a rapid heat-up feature and is designed to do this.
See the Radiant surface elements section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "The rapid heat-up feature activated."

symptoms.symptom: “F” and a number appear in the display and the cooktop produces an audible sound

causes.label: You have a fault code.
remedies: Write down the “F” and the number and touch the CONTROL LOCK pad.
See the Fault code section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "You have a fault code."
